declarations.documentation:
One model step over the conversation + tool schemas — the provider seam. A provider serves this for
the extent of a continuation (`use <some provider>.provider(...)`). The reply is an outcome and never a
throw: `inferred(result)` carries the step and its token accounting, `inference_failed(error)` the
failure the provider gave up on — so each loop decides at its own perform site whether to absorb the
failure or re-raise it.
declarations.name: infer_step

anyOf.description: call_turn: A conversation turn recording the model's tool-call batch — replayed so the next step shows the model what it already asked for.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
tool_call: One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key), @ref@ is
the call's opaque correlation handle, and @args@ is the model's argument object as a parsed value,
dispatched straight through `reflection.call_agent`, whose boundary turns any replayed `$katari_ref` into
the `file` it denotes.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: The correlation handle of one tool call: a single opaque token, minted by the provider that parsed the
model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn and on the result that answers it. What it holds is
the provider's own business, and nothing above the provider reads it: a result and its call correlate by
carrying the same value.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: result_turn: A conversation turn carrying the results of a tool-call batch.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
tool_result: A tool's output for the model, carrying the @ref@ of the call it answers so it round-trips as a function
response, and that call's tool @name@ so a wire that keys its responses by name has it to hand. @files@
are the `file` values found in the result: @text@ already shows their `$katari_ref` handles, and a
provider that can inline their content does so while the result is fresh.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: The correlation handle of one tool call: a single opaque token, minted by the provider that parsed the
model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn and on the result that answers it. What it holds is
the provider's own business, and nothing above the provider reads it: a result and its call correlate by
carrying the same value.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description:
turn: One turn in a conversation: who spoke, what they said, and any files attached to it. Files ride as blob
handles and each provider decides when to inline their content. @author@ is the optional opaque end-user
tag of a user turn (e.g. a hashed chat-user id), never shown to the model — a provider whose API has an
abuse-attribution field lifts the newest user turn's author into it (`ai.attribution`). `null` (the
default) means the turn is not attributable to an end user.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
model_role: Whose turn this is: the model's own — text it produced on an earlier step and that is replayed to it as
its own words. The wire token differs per provider; which one goes out is the adapter's decision, made by
matching this sum.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
user_role: Whose turn this is: the caller's side of the conversation — a person's message, a system framing turn,
a background report, a turn the loop synthesized.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
agent_metadata: The public metadata of one callable: its (qualified) name, its `@"..."` description, and the JSON
Schemas of its input, output and requests — each schema a plain document value, ready to embed in an AI
tool list. A local (closure) callable has an empty name.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

description.description: The `@"..."` documentation text; empty when undocumented.

input.description: The input record's JSON Schema, as a document value.

name.description: The qualified name; empty for a local closure.

output.description: The output's JSON Schema, as a document value.

requests.description: The requests' schemas: one { name, input, output } object per request the callable may perform.

anyOf.description:
inference_failed: One model step's outcome failure: the provider gave up — a transient error past its retry budget, or a
fatal status / malformed body. Carried as a value so a loop handles it at its own perform site.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the provider can name — the arm that lets a provider carry its own failure as a
value instead of earning an arm here. @source@ names the producer, @message@ is the one human-readable
line, @transient@ is the producer's own verdict on whether a retry could help (`is_transient` reads it),
and @detail@ is the producer's own typed datum.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

error.description: The step error the provider surfaced.

anyOf.description:
inferred: One model step's outcome success: the provider produced a step. Generic over the payload so
`infer_step` and `infer_object` share one sum shape.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

The step the provider produced.

into it, rather than being guessed about here.

declarations.checkedType: agent(attempt: agent(value: null) -> T2 with throw[provider_error | missing_secret | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error | server_error] | io, attempts: integer, base_milliseconds: number) -> (inference_failed | inferred[T2]) with throw[missing_secret | server_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
One bounded retry loop over one @attempt@ agent — the control flow and the catching every provider
shares. Run @attempt@ up to @attempts@ times with its `step_error` folded to a value by `prelude.catch`:
a completed attempt answers `inferred(result)`; a transient error sleeps `backoff_milliseconds` and tries
again while there is budget; a fatal one, or a transient one past the budget, answers
`inference_failed(error)` as a value, because that is what the seam promises its caller.

@attempt@ therefore throws rather than catching — it is a plain thunk around the provider's own call. A
credential failure is not a step failure and passes straight through to the app's supervisor
(`env.missing_secret`, `oauth.server_error`). @attempts@ below 1 is a configuration defect and answers as
one: a non-transient `provider_error` from this middleware naming the knob.

declarations.documentation:
Tool: read a file that is in this conversation — an image, a PDF, or a text document. Pass the file's
handle object; a bare {"$katari_ref": "<id>"} suffices (copy the id from the conversation). A text
document (`text/*`, JSON, XML, CSV) comes back as text, cut at a cap with an explicit truncation marker
when it is long; an image, a PDF, audio or video comes back as the file itself, which the model
connection places in your context if its API accepts that type — so if the content does not appear, say
you cannot see it rather than guessing. A content type nothing can read (an archive, an office document,
an unrecorded type) comes back as a note saying exactly that, and reporting it is then the correct
answer.

then step against the ambient provider up to @max_steps@ times, dispatching a batch of tool calls

declarations.documentation:
Find the tool whose metadata name is the model's pick and invoke it by value via
`reflection.call_agent`, whose delegation boundary validates the model's args against the tool's schema
and turns any replayed `$katari_ref` into the `file` it denotes. Every way a call can go wrong — a
hallucinated name, a tool that panics, a tool's own typed throw, malformed args, and a call that outruns
@budget_milliseconds@ (raced via `time.with_deadline`, the late call cancelled) — is fed back to the
model as an error result it corrects from, and none of them reaches the app root; a thrown payload
carrying a string `message` field is shown as that line, anything else as the payload's JSON. Each also
yields a `tool_event`, and the result's `file` values are collected off the result tree so the provider
can show them to the model.
declarations.name: dispatch_one

@policy.keep_recent@ elements, extended to a clean turn boundary) is summarized by one tool-less model
step under @policy.prompt@, and the summary replaces it as a single opening turn. A history that is all
tail comes back unchanged. Exported on its own so a hand-rolled loop can compact too.

items.description:
agent_metadata: The public metadata of one callable: its (qualified) name, its `@"..."` description, and the JSON
Schemas of its input, output and requests — each schema a plain document value, ready to embed in an AI
tool list. A local (closure) callable has an empty name.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

description.description: The `@"..."` documentation text; empty when undocumented.

input.description: The input record's JSON Schema, as a document value.

name.description: The qualified name; empty for a local closure.

output.description: The output's JSON Schema, as a document value.

requests.description: The requests' schemas: one { name, input, output } object per request the callable may perform.

anyOf.description:
inference_failed: One model step's outcome failure: the provider gave up — a transient error past its retry budget, or a
fatal status / malformed body. Carried as a value so a loop handles it at its own perform site.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the provider can name — the arm that lets a provider carry its own failure as a
value instead of earning an arm here. @source@ names the producer, @message@ is the one human-readable
line, @transient@ is the producer's own verdict on whether a retry could help (`is_transient` reads it),
and @detail@ is the producer's own typed datum.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

error.description: The step error the provider surfaced.

anyOf.description:
inferred: One model step's outcome success: the provider produced a step. Generic over the payload so
`infer_step` and `infer_object` share one sum shape.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

The step the provider produced.

step_result: What a provider returns for one model step: the decision plus its token accounting.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is

anyOf.description:

403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

replayed answers the same way.

declarations.signature: agent closing_step(history: array[types.message], events: array[tool_event] ?= []) -> turn_result

declarations.checkedType: agent(conversation: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E5 lacks race_settled}], unbounded_tool_names?: array[string]) -> (failed_turn | session_turn) with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool] | {...E5 lacks throw | race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
The turn loop — advance @conversation@ by one model turn and hand back a value either way: up to
@max_steps@ steps against the ambient provider, tool batches dispatched in parallel, the model's reply
appended as a model turn, and the last step's `input + output` carried out as the context measurement
(each step's input covers the whole context, so only the freshest figure is the occupancy). Budget spent,
one forced tool-less close commits to an answer; a provider failure at any step returns `failed_turn`
rather than unwinding, so an app-owned event loop absorbs it as one match arm. This is the package's one
loop — the one-shot calls and `serve_observations` are both compositions over it.

An empty final comes back empty, and nothing here second-guesses it: a caller that wants the model
prompted for a real answer says so in the conversation it passes.
declarations.name: take_turn

parameters.documentation:
The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds — every call races it via `time.with_deadline`, and a timeout
comes back to the model as an error result. `null` (the default) sets no deadline.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation:
The metadata names of tools exempt from the deadline race — the human-latency ones: an approval-gated
adapter that blocks on an operator's click, an MCP call that may park on an OAuth authorization. A
deadline bounds machine latency, and a pending ask is visible in the admin surface while it waits.
Defaults to none — every tool stays under the budget.
parameters.label: unbounded_tool_names

declarations.signature: agent take_turn[effect E](conversation: array[types.message], tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null ?= null, unbounded_tool_names: array[string] ?= []) -> turn_result

declarations.documentation:
The event→model channel: a background fiber (an always-on source such as a chat watcher, a started
watch, or another agent's `mail`) pushes @content@ from @source@ into the model's context.
Fire-and-forget — a fiber only reports, and the serving handler injects the report as a user turn,
advances the conversation and routes the reply to its `deliver_to`. @files@ ride the injection turn's
`files` slot and @author@ its `author`, so the triggered turn's requests carry the right
abuse-attribution metadata.

@hop@ has no default: it is a fact about the message — how many agent-to-agent relays it has already
made — so it is carried rather than guessed. Write `hop = 0` for anything a person or a clock sent (a
chat message, a cron tick, a watch report, a startup line), 1 for a first-hop send, 2 for the reply to
one, and `inbound_provenance().hop + 1` in a tool that relays.
declarations.name: observation

parameters.documentation: Which fiber is reporting (e.g. "discord:<channel>", "mail:core"); it labels the report's injection turn.
parameters.label: source

parameters.documentation: The report to inject into the model's context.
parameters.label: content

parameters.documentation: How many agent-to-agent hops this message has already made; 0 for anything a person or a clock sent. No default, on purpose — see above.
parameters.label: hop

parameters.documentation: Any files attached to the report (a Discord / Slack attachment), injected on the report's turn so the provider inlines them for the model; defaults to none.
parameters.label: files

parameters.documentation: The opaque end-user tag of the human behind this report (e.g. a hashed chat-user id), or `null` for a system report (a scheduled tick).
parameters.label: author

content.description: The report to inject into the model's context.

declarations.signature: request observation(source: string, content: string, hop: integer, files: array[file] ?= [], author: string | null ?= null) -> null

declarations.documentation:
The provenance of the observation this conversation is serving right now: @origin@ is the observation's
`source` verbatim and @hop@ is its `hop`. Served by `serve_observations` for the extent of one dispatch —
a tool set is assembled once for the whole conversation, so a tool cannot close over the message it is
answering, and this is the frame that holds it. A tool reads both as values instead of parsing them back
out of the injected turn's prose. A program with no serving handler beneath it simply has no handler for
this, so the capability is visible in a tool's own effect row.
declarations.name: inbound_provenance

declarations.documentation:
The arrivals a conversation is holding because the model was not answering: @messages@ is the bounded
tail and @dropped@ counts what fell off the front. It lives beside the conversation rather than in it,
which is what makes an outage cost the conversation nothing. Internal to `serve_observations`.
declarations.name: backlog

parameters.documentation: The newest held arrivals, oldest first.
parameters.label: messages

parameters.documentation: How many older ones the bound discarded.
parameters.label: dropped

declarations.checkedType: agent(kind: needs_operator | waits_out, messages: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]) -> array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]
declarations.documentation:
The shed decision, made once from the outage classification: a refused call's messages lose their
attachments, a passing failure's messages keep every one. `needs_operator` is exactly the family that
repeats deterministically, and an attachment is the one part of a request whose acceptability an app
cannot test before sending. The imprecision inside that family is accepted with open eyes, because a shed
attachment is a noted, re-askable loss while a poisoned conversation is one nothing revives. Internal to
`serve_observations`.
declarations.name: shed_refused

parameters.documentation: What the failure said about who can end it.
parameters.label: kind

parameters.documentation: The messages that rode the failed call.
parameters.label: messages

anyOf.description:
needs_operator: What a failed step says about who can end the outage: a person must act. A 400 (a spent credit balance,
a model the provider no longer serves), a 401 or 403 (a wrong, revoked or under-privileged key) and a 404
do not heal with time, so @remedy@ carries the one clause that turns an evening of silence into a
five-minute fix.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

remedy.description: What to check, in one clause.

anyOf.description:
waits_out: What a failed step says about who can end the outage: nobody — it is the kind that passes. A rate
limit, a 5xx, a dropped connection, a reply the provider could not make sense of. The provider has already
spent its retry budget on it, so the only jobs left are to stop hammering and to say nothing an operator
cannot act on.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

declarations.signature: agent hold_arrival(held: backlog, message: types.message, retention: integer) -> backlog

declarations.documentation:
The one line that stands in for what a backlog's bound discarded, or no line at all when it discarded
nothing. It is derived from the count on every attempt rather than appended to the stored conversation,
so an outage spanning ten failed probes still produces one line; the turn that answers bakes it in and
clears the count. Internal to `serve_observations`.

declarations.documentation:
The conversation a turn leaves behind, with one line appended when the turn ended with text that
nothing delivered — the case a resident with no @deliver_to@ is in on every turn it chose to speak. A
blank final gains nothing: ending silently is a legitimate move under this protocol. The line is the only
condition tested, because who the text was for is the model's judgement. Internal to
`serve_observations`.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the provider can name — the arm that lets a provider carry its own failure as a
value instead of earning an arm here. @source@ names the producer, @message@ is the one human-readable
line, @transient@ is the producer's own verdict on whether a retry could help (`is_transient` reads it),
and @detail@ is the producer's own typed datum.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call

replayed answers the same way.

declarations.documentation:
Advance one served conversation by one observation — the whole of a resident's per-message behaviour.
The report injects as a user turn onto the stored conversation plus whatever the backlog holds, and one
`take_turn` runs. Answered: a non-blank reply goes to @deliver_to@, the backlog clears and an over-budget
conversation compacts. Refused by an open breaker, or failed: the report is filed into the bounded
backlog and the stored conversation stays frozen, so an outage costs it nothing — and a failure
additionally sheds the attachments of the call the provider refused, across the whole backlog. A failed
turn's partial tool work is discarded rather than preserved, so the recovery turn re-drives the model
with no record of it and a non-idempotent tool can run a second time for one report.

For the extent of the dispatch it serves `inbound_provenance` with this observation's `source` and
`hop`. Internal to `serve_observations`.
declarations.name: advance_resident

declarations.documentation:
Serve a resident conversation for the extent of @continuation@ — the serving mechanism this package
offers. One conversation behind one handler var, each `observation` advancing it and a non-blank reply
leaving through @deliver_to@; every resident behaviour comes with it (see the resident section above).

The continuation forks the conversation's sources and typically never returns (a `region.watch`). Every
fiber runs under that watch, so the ambient provider and any @E@ handlers are installed by the caller
above this line, where they cover all of them.

`observation` is served by the innermost install in scope, so one install serves one conversation; do not
install it twice in one dynamic extent, where the inner install shadows the outer and the second agent
receives nothing. Several agents are several fibers: `ai.route` + `ai.spawn` is the product form, and
`resident` is one AI's whole body for a program assembling it by hand. The providers serve `infer_step`
from a parallel handler of their own, so one provider install covers every AI in the program and no two
of their model calls serialize against each other.
declarations.name: serve_observations

The shared scope marker of every `ai` mailbox, so that a resident's mailbox and a delivery site agree on
one type without either naming the other. A sender discharges it with one
`region.provide[ai.mail_scope, ai.observation]` — a nursery opened purely to hold the stamp, which is what
`route` calls its franking — and can then fork into any resident's mailbox handle. The merge is
type-level only: a fork routes by the handle's own runtime scope identity, minted freshly per install, so
no fiber can be delivered to the wrong nursery.
declarations.name: mail_scope

declarations.documentation:
A resident announcing its mailbox — the handshake by which an AI becomes addressable: performed once by
`resident` from inside its own `provide`, and answered by `route`, which keeps the `record[mailbox]` every
`mail` looks up. It is a request rather than a return value because a resident never returns.

It is also the door into the route's table: a program that forks a resident of its own performs this from
inside that fiber, and the route files the handle beside the AIs it spawned. `mail(to = ...)` then finds
it and the sender cannot tell the two apart; only `dismiss` can, because the route can only cancel a
fiber it forked.
declarations.name: register

declarations.documentation:
The delivery fiber: one report carried into a resident's mailbox. Fork it — never call it: forked into
the addressee's handle — `region.fork(nursery = box, task = ai.deliver, argument = { source = "mail:core",
content = text, hop = 1 })` — it runs in the addressee's nursery, performs one `observation`, and settles,
while a direct call compiles and performs the observation in the caller's own position instead;
`route`'s `mail` clause is this fork plus the table lookup.

It is a named agent taking plain data because a cross-nursery fork carries its task's captured
environment into the target's instance, and a named agent captures nothing. Its parameters are
`observation`'s exactly: @files@ and @author@ may be omitted, @hop@ may not. Delivery is at-most-once —
a fork into a nursery that has already died panics; fold the fork with `supervise.once` +
`supervise.signal_panics` where a lost message must be noticed, as `route`'s `mail` clause does.

declarations.documentation:
One AI's whole body, as a task to fork — the mechanism under `spawn`. Most programs write
`ai.spawn(name = "core", tools = core_tools, max_steps = 16)` instead; reach for the fork itself when the
AI needs something wrapped around it that the route cannot pass through (a provider install of its own, a
facility only this AI may reach). It still joins the route's table, because `register` is what puts it
there.

It bundles: its own mailbox nursery, separate from the one it was forked into and announced with
`register(name, box)`; @persona@ recomputed at every model step through `with_context`; `serve_observations`
with every knob passed through; the mailbox's own `region.watch`; and, when @workspace@ is given, the
whole fiber inside one `store.workspace`.

It raises `infer_step` (to the ambient provider, installed outside the root watch), `register` (to the
route, once at startup), and the mailbox's `region.crashed` / `region.failed` (to the root watch, where a
mail fiber's death is reported under its fork name). Its tools', @persona@'s and @deliver_to@'s own
effects @E@ pass through untouched and must be covered by the root nursery's ceiling.

Instantiate `E` explicitly at the fork — `ai.resident[io | my_request]` — because a fork takes the task as
a value, not as a call, so nothing infers its type arguments there. @name@ is what mail addresses it as,
not the fiber's name tag; giving the fork the same string is worth the keystrokes when a `crashed` event
has to be matched to an AI.

declarations.documentation:
Hire one AI: fork a `resident` into the route's nursery under @name@ and — once it announces its
mailbox — its @sources@ beside it. Answers `spawned(id)`, or `already_running(id)` when the name is taken.

Spell the effect argument: `ai.spawn[io | discord.send](...)`. @E@ is the row this program's own agents
run under, and nothing infers it at a perform site — a request's type arguments are not recovered from
its arguments the way an agent call's are, so an unspelled `ai.spawn(...)` is a `K3016` — or, when a
tool's own row happens to fit, a confusing `K3001` about a request the row does not allow.

Sources start at the handshake and not at this call, so a source that mails on its very first breath
cannot post to an address that does not exist yet.

Everything in the argument record travels into a fiber the caller does not own, so `tools`, `persona`,
`deliver_to` and `sources` are named top-level agents over plain data: a named agent captures nothing,
while a closure carries the calling fiber's environment with it.

declarations.documentation:
Open the route for the extent of @continuation@ — the `let root = use ai.route()` line. It opens the
nursery the AIs live in, hands @continuation@ its handle (to be watched as the program's tail), and
serves `spawn` / `mail` / `dismiss`, the `register` handshake the residents announce themselves with, and
the two ending events, which it uses to forget a dead AI before re-raising them outward unchanged.

The route re-performs the ending events outward, so your own handlers — the provider, the breaker,
whatever serves your tools' effects, and `region.crashed` / `region.failed` — are installed above this
line, where those re-performs reach them; one installed below this line sits below the re-performs and
never sees them.

An AI becomes addressable when its `register` handshake is served, and a fiber's escalations are held
durably until the watch is up. The first report to an AI therefore comes from something that runs after
`region.watch(nursery = root)`: a `sources` entry (forked at the handshake), a tool, or one of your own
handlers. A `mail` performed before that answers `no_recipient`, and nothing is retried.

Put a restart at the altitude of what died. A `crashed` names a dead fiber whose region is alive, so a
re-hiring handler stands inside this provider's extent (below this line, above the watch), where a
`spawn` reaches the route; above this line is outside the region, and a `spawn` there escalates past the
route to the run root as an open question. An ending travels both altitudes in order — the route evicts,
an in-region re-hire handler acts, the outer notice speaks — so a re-hire handler re-performs the event
outward first and spawns after.

It carries the four store operations whatever your AIs actually do, because `spawn`'s `workspace` option
means a resident may re-perform them and an effect row is static; read them as "reaches the store".
There is no pending queue for mail to an AI that has not registered yet (the caller gets `no_recipient`
and decides), no broadcast and no priorities: those are routing policy, and a program with an opinion
writes it over the mechanism layer this one is built from.
declarations.name: route

declarations.checkedType: agent(continuation: agent(value: null) -> T16 with infer_step | E17, inject: agent(value: null) -> string with infer_step | E17) -> T16 with infer_step | E17
declarations.documentation:
Middleware over the seam: at every `infer_step`, insert @inject@'s freshly computed text as a user turn
just before the newest user turn, and re-perform outward to the ambient provider. Install it inside the
provider (the provider's `use` first, then this). An empty injection skips the extra turn; the injected
turn is never part of the conversation a loop persists, since it is derived fresh each step.
`infer_object` passes through un-injected.

The note lands at the end of the conversation's stable region: an ambient note is by definition the part
that changes, every model API reuses a repeated request prefix only while it stays byte-identical, and a
turn's tool loop only appends after the newest user turn.
declarations.name: with_context

declarations.documentation:
Classify a failed step by who can end it. An `http.auth_error` is always a person's job — 401 and 403
both name a credential nobody but an operator can replace — while an `http.api_error` needs its status
read, because that arm holds a 400 (act) beside a 429 (wait). A `json.parse_error` and a `provider_error`
land in `waits_out` deliberately: they are not transient either, but there is no lever to hand an operator
for them. Everything else waits, `http.fetch_error` included.

value instead of earning an arm here. @source@ names the producer, @message@ is the one human-readable
line, @transient@ is the producer's own verdict on whether a retry could help (`is_transient` reads it),
and @detail@ is the producer's own typed datum.

anyOf.description:

not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

anyOf.description:

403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

threshold it opens ready — @next_probe@ is @now@, so the next step to arrive probes immediately. An

from this failure.

not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

declarations.checkedType: agent(kind: needs_operator | waits_out, now: number, policy: breaker_policy, succeeded: boolean) -> (breaker_closed | breaker_held | breaker_opened) with exclusive
declarations.documentation:
Fold one step's outcome into the stored breaker state, atomically, and say whether it flipped. This is
the critical section: it re-reads the state (the decision to call was made from a read outside it, which
may be one step stale), applies this outcome, writes it back and answers the transition, all inside
`store.exclusive`. @on_transition@ is called by the caller on the answer, because a critical section that
could call out would be one holding a network.
declarations.name: record_step

declarations.documentation:
Middleware over the seam: install one breaker for every model call in @continuation@'s dynamic extent —
every resident, every hand-rolled `take_turn` — inside the provider (the provider's `use` first, then
this), so a refused step never reaches the provider at all.

@failure_threshold@ consecutive failed steps open it; while open, `infer_step` answers
`inference_failed(breaker_refusal_error(...))` without calling out, except for the one probe step per
interval that tests for recovery. @on_transition@ fires on the state change and nowhere else: once on the
way out, once on the way back. Where those two lines go and how they read is the app's — the sink gets the
`outage_kind`, and `outage_line` / `recovery_line` are the wordings this package suggests.

The handler is parallel and the state lives in the store (at `breaker_key`, in whatever workspace this is
installed in), so several AIs' model calls do not serialize behind one FIFO and a program that restarts
into a standing outage still knows about it. `infer_object` passes through un-broken.

declarations.documentation:
Serve `ai.infer_step` over Anthropic for the extent of the continuation:
`use anthropic.provider(source = credentials.env(key = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))`.
A step's provider failure (`ai.step_error`) is handed back as an `ai.inference_failed` outcome; a
transient one (a 429, a 5xx, a dropped connection) is first retried with exponential backoff, up to
@retry_attempts@ attempts from @retry_base_milliseconds@. Prompt caching is on and needs no argument:
every step marks two `cache_control` breakpoints, one at the end of the tools+@system@ prefix and one at
the end of the conversation, so a tool loop re-reads what it already sent at a tenth of the price. The
prompt-caching section of this module says what silently undoes it.

the call's opaque correlation handle, and @args@ is the model's argument object as a parsed value,
dispatched straight through `reflection.call_agent`, whose boundary turns any replayed `$katari_ref` into

model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn and on the result that answers it. What it holds is
the provider's own business, and nothing above the provider reads it: a result and its call correlate by
carrying the same value.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: result_turn: A conversation turn carrying the results of a tool-call batch.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

response, and that call's tool @name@ so a wire that keys its responses by name has it to hand. @files@
are the `file` values found in the result: @text@ already shows their `$katari_ref` handles, and a

The structured-output request body: @schema@ as the input schema of one synthetic tool with
`tool_choice` pinned to it. It takes the same prefix breakpoint as a step, but no conversation breakpoint
— an object step states its own context and is not re-sent with a growing history, so marking its messages
would pay a cache write nothing ever reads.

declarations.signature: agent anthropic_parse_step(parsed: unknown, map: wire_names.name_map) -> types.step

declarations.documentation:
The step's token accounting off the response's `usage`. The context a step read splits across
`input_tokens` and the cache counters (`cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens`), so the
occupancy is their sum and an absent field reads as 0. A warm step therefore reports most of its context
under `cache_read_input_tokens`, which is how a run trace shows the cache working.
declarations.name: anthropic_usage

parameters.documentation: The parsed response document.
parameters.label: parsed

output.description:
usage: One step's token accounting, as the provider's API reported it. @input_tokens@ counts the whole context
the step consumed, so the freshest step's figure is the session's current occupancy — figures across steps
do not add. @output_tokens@ counts what the model generated on the step.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

the call's opaque correlation handle, and @args@ is the model's argument object as a parsed value,
dispatched straight through `reflection.call_agent`, whose boundary turns any replayed `$katari_ref` into
the `file` it denotes.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: The correlation handle of one tool call: a single opaque token, minted by the provider that parsed the
model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn and on the result that answers it. What it holds is
the provider's own business, and nothing above the provider reads it: a result and its call correlate by
carrying the same value.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: step_final: One inference step's decision: a final reply text for the user.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

usage.description:
usage: One step's token accounting, as the provider's API reported it. @input_tokens@ counts the whole context
the step consumed, so the freshest step's figure is the session's current occupancy — figures across steps
do not add. @output_tokens@ counts what the model generated on the step.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
missing_secret: No secret env entry is set under @key@. Thrown by `get_secret` — catch it to fall back in-program
(`use handler { request throw(error: env.missing_secret) -> never { ... } }`, or fold it to a value with
`prelude.catch`).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

key.description: The key that had no secret entry.

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
server_error: The OAuth token could not be resolved for a TRANSIENT reason — a network error, or the token endpoint
failing (5xx) while refreshing. Thrown by `token`; a retried call re-resolves. (A credential that needs
a human to (re)authorize is never a throw: the run pauses on an authorization escalation instead.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

synthetic tool and `tool_choice` pins the model to it, so the decoded object arrives already parsed as the
tool_use block's `input` — no special API surface, every Claude model. A reply with no tool_use block
throws `json.parse_error`.

declarations.documentation:
Serve `ai.infer_step` over Gemini for the extent of the continuation:
`use gemini.provider(source = credentials.env(key = "GEMINI_API_KEY"))`.
A step's provider failure (`ai.step_error`) is handed back as an `ai.inference_failed` outcome; a
transient one (a 429, a 5xx, a dropped connection) is first retried with exponential backoff, up to
@retry_attempts@ attempts from @retry_base_milliseconds@. Gemini caches a repeated prefix implicitly, so
nothing here asks for caching.
declarations.name: provider

parameters.documentation:
The generateContent model id. Defaults to `gemini-3.5-flash`: the flash tier is the general-purpose
workhorse of the series this module is written against, and a default should be the model a program can
afford to run at every step.
parameters.label: model

parameters.documentation: Where the API key lives (env key or oauth name); resolved at each request, so a rotation lands mid-run.
parameters.label: source

parameters.documentation: An optional system instruction, sent as `systemInstruction`; `null` (the default) sends none. "" is NOT the way to say none — it sends an empty instruction.
parameters.label: system

parameters.documentation: How many times a transient step (a 429 / 5xx / dropped connection) is attempted before its error becomes an `inference_failed` outcome.
parameters.label: retry_attempts

parameters.documentation: The first backoff delay in milliseconds, doubled per retry (capped at one minute).
parameters.label: retry_base_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: generationConfig.maxOutputTokens — the per-step output cap; `null` (the default) sends none.
parameters.label: max_output_tokens

parameters.documentation: generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget — bounds the thought tokens a thinking model may burn before the answer; `null` (the default) sends none.
parameters.label: thinking_budget

parameters.documentation: The computation to run with `ai.infer_step` / `ai.infer_object` served.
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.documentation:
A file's content as an inlineData part — what lets the model actually see the file. The `data` slot
holds the file value placed directly into the tree; `http.json` reads its bytes and base64s them in place
only at the send boundary, so the content never rides the value plane.
declarations.name: gemini_inline_part

parameters.label: attachment

parameters.documentation: Its recorded content type, which `generateContent` takes as the part's `mimeType`.
parameters.label: mime_type

declarations.documentation:
A file as its `$katari_ref` handle note part — the resting representation, and the affordance the model
replays into any tool it holds that takes a file.
declarations.name: gemini_handle_part

declarations.documentation:
Whether `generateContent` accepts @mime_type@ as an `inlineData` part: the union of the documented
image, audio and video format lists, plus `application/pdf`. One match over all four families, because the
part is the same shape whichever family a type belongs to, and each family is wider than what the model
decodes. `ai.normalized_content_type` has already resolved the confirmed aliases.
declarations.name: gemini_inline_media_type

parameters.documentation: The file's normalized content type.
parameters.label: mime_type

declarations.documentation:
An inlinable file's parts: the handle note and the `inlineData` part when Gemini accepts the mime type,
and the unreadable note when it does not. An unaccepted type 400s the step and takes the turn with it,
where the note costs the model one honest sentence and the conversation goes on.
declarations.name: gemini_media_parts

parameters.label: attachment

parameters.label: mime_type

declarations.documentation:
One attached file as the parts it becomes — the per-file dispatch over `ai.file_kind`. An image, a PDF,
audio and video all reach `gemini_media_parts`, because that one `inlineData` part is Gemini's whole
multimodal surface and it is the accepted media type, not the family, that decides whether the content can
ride; a textual file rides as text, capped; an opaque type says it cannot be read.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the provider can name — the arm that lets a provider carry its own failure as a
value instead of earning an arm here. @source@ names the producer, @message@ is the one human-readable
line, @transient@ is the producer's own verdict on whether a retry could help (`is_transient` reads it),
and @detail@ is the producer's own typed datum.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

declarations.documentation:
Serve `ai.infer_step` over OpenAI for the extent of the continuation:
`use openai.provider(source = credentials.env(key = "OPENAI_API_KEY"))`.
A step's provider failure (`ai.step_error`) is handed back as an `ai.inference_failed` outcome; a
transient one (a 429, a 5xx, a dropped connection) is first retried with exponential backoff, up to
@retry_attempts@ attempts from @retry_base_milliseconds@. OpenAI caches a repeated prefix automatically,
so nothing here asks for caching.
declarations.name: provider

anyOf.description:

403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

replayed answers the same way.

tool_call: One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key), @ref@ is
the call's opaque correlation handle, and @args@ is the model's argument object as a parsed value,
dispatched straight through `reflection.call_agent`, whose boundary turns any replayed `$katari_ref` into
the `file` it denotes.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: The correlation handle of one tool call: a single opaque token, minted by the provider that parsed the
model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn and on the result that answers it. What it holds is
the provider's own business, and nothing above the provider reads it: a result and its call correlate by
carrying the same value.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: step_final: One inference step's decision: a final reply text for the user.

usage: One step's token accounting, as the provider's API reported it. @input_tokens@ counts the whole context
the step consumed, so the freshest step's figure is the session's current occupancy — figures across steps
do not add. @output_tokens@ counts what the model generated on the step.

declarations.documentation:
A deterministic two-way mapping between a tool's real (qualified) name and the shortened name a provider
sends on the wire. @real_to_wire@ is keyed by the qualified name (encoding a declaration or a replayed
call turn), @wire_to_real@ by the wire name (reversing the model's pick); both are total over one step's
tools.

declarations.documentation:
Fold a wire name onto a qualified name: every character outside the `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` alphabet these APIs
share — the dot of a qualified name above all — folds to `_`, and the result is capped at their
64-character limit.
declarations.name: sanitize_name

parameters.documentation: The qualified tool name.
parameters.label: name

name.description: The qualified tool name.

declarations.documentation:
Disambiguate a colliding wire name with an ordinal suffix (`_2`, `_3`, …), reserving room so the
result still fits the 64-character cap.
declarations.name: suffixed_name

parameters.documentation: The colliding base wire name.
parameters.label: base

parameters.documentation: The 1-based ordinal.
parameters.label: index

declarations.signature: agent suffixed_name(base: string, index: integer) -> string

declarations.documentation:
Choose a free wire name for @real@ given the wire names already @taken@: its sanitized form, or the
first free ordinal-suffixed form when sanitizing or truncation collapsed two qualified names onto one
token. The suffix is decided by @taken@'s size, so the choice is deterministic.
declarations.name: assign_wire_name
